Visit West Hill Park
Little Griffins to become an all year round setting and welcome two year olds
Visit Us
Welcome to West Hill Park
West Hill Park School, Prep & Nursery in Hampshire
Nestled in a unique rural setting within easy reach of Portsmouth and Southampton, West Hill Park is more than just a school, we are a vibrant community where every child has the chance to flourish.
Head’s Welcome
West Hill Park is an independent day and boarding prep school and nursery for children aged 2–13, set in 28 acres in Titchfield, Hampshire, within easy reach of Portsmouth and Southampton. We are a school where curiosity is unleashed. Our beautiful woodland classroom, riding school, theatre, sports fields, and more create endless possibilities for exploration and growth…
Discover West Hill Park School
Nursery
Pre-Prep
Prep
Boarding Life
We provide our boarders with a warm, supportive environment where they can grow and flourish with family values at heart.

Nursery Ethos
Little Griffins
Little Griffins is our wonderful Early Years setting. We pride ourselves on creating an engaging, calm and tranquil environment where children can build their own play using authentic materials that mirror the home.
We want the children to have a love of learning through curiosity, opportunities and experiences and within a safe and nurturing environment.
Children who join Little Griffins have the opportunity to experience all the school has to offer, from swimming in our on-site pool to specialist music classes, French, PE and the opportunity to take riding lessons at the on-site stables.
They have their own playground, but enjoy lunch in the main dining hall, with beautifully prepared fresh meals, real knives and forks and open cups.
Children are welcome from 2 years old.
Wild Griffins
Wild Griffins is our 100% outdoor Forest School provision. Led by Miss Allen our Forest School Leader. Set within 25 acres of grounds, Wild Griffins has its own designated area, with a Yurt in place for the most extreme weather conditions. Wild Griffins has space for 12 children.
Children in a forest school environment experience nature first-hand, they witness the changing of the seasons and get caught up in the wonder those changes bring about. Our Wild Griffins are able to harness the power of the outdoors and use it to help them understand science, numeracy, literacy, working as part of a team, problem-solving, risk-taking and so much more.
Children are welcome from 2.5 years old.
Our Early Years provision encompasses the very best of Prep School life, and an exceptional outdoor Forest School Nursery with Wild Griffins. Children are welcome to mix and match their days across the two settings during term time, with Little Griffins open all year round.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Aims - West Hill Park
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Aims
West Hill Park is a caring community that inspires every child to have a love of learning through curiosity, opportunities and experiences and within a safe and nurturing environment.
Curriculum – to deliver an exciting, challenging and stimulating curriculum that engages every child and provide the skills needed for their future and an ever-changing world.
Pastoral Care – to develop and care for the physical, social and mental well-being of every child through a supportive environment that allows the individual’s voice to be valued.
Values – to have positive relationships with all members of the WHP community built on mutual respect, kindness and good manners.
Community – to allow opportunities for children to engage and positively contribute to the local community and society more widely.
Every child has an area in which they can excel, and the diverse curriculum and enrichment activities we offer gives them just this opportunity. We focus on nurturing three main pillars of character and emotional intelligence.
The tremendous diversity of opportunity we offer allows each of our pupils to find a space in which they can excel. Be it in the science lab, learning an instrument, a new artistic creation, performing in the latest stage production, forest school adventures, or on the sports pitch, every child can find the success that builds vital confidence.
The support and encouragement our children receive from our close community and excellent pastoral care help foster a learning environment where children are prepared to push the edge of their comfort zone, be it through extension work in the classroom, or challenges outside it. We value effort, kindness and positive attitude above all, and in this setting a child is unafraid to take risks to fulfil their potential.
Respect, caring and empathy are critical to our happy boarding and day school community. They are absolutely key to our core pillars of learning and behaviour.
Every aspect of a culture that creates a contented study environment for the child must be based on a generosity of spirit that is highly valued by the peer group.
These close and supportive interpersonal relationships are encouraged through activities that complement our study and developmental objectives. Older years caring and working with the younger is given priority in our vertically structured academic and extra-curricular house events, while the outdoor modules in our curriculum are very appropriate for children to learn to cooperate and enjoy each other’s company in new and challenging surroundings.
Thriving when challenged, and flexibility in a changing environment, are key skills for the next step in our children’s learning journey.
As our pupils progress, there will sometimes be bumps in the road, and our aim is to guide them on this journey. The inevitable misstep elicits a sympathetic response, enabling them to react positively and constructively. Mistakes are an opportunity for growth, and we create an environment where the children feel safe to take a risk. Respect for and empathy with the children, and a support system with staff that know them well, help them to rebound with spirit and learn from the experience. Our curriculum, both indoor and outdoor, is built around the individual student’s strengths and weaknesses, tailored to set the achievable goals that will motivate, enthuse and reward.
As important as the content of the curriculum, are the learning skills so important to taking advantage of the opportunities on offer and to fulfil a child’s potential in life’s journey.
Curious and Expressive
A love of learning and a will to discover is perhaps the greatest gift to a child, developing a character flexible and content in a quickly changing world.
In Early Years, where our children follow a curiosity based curriculum, they are given a wide range of authentic real life resources with which to create and discover, fostering critical thinking and the urge to explore.
Pupils are always encouraged to put forward their opinions and ask questions. We appreciate and celebrate the diversity of our children who feel confident to express themselves in different environments. To cater to this, we offer a range of opportunities to present to a supportive group, whether it be on the stage, in the classroom or in our beautiful grounds.
The ability to both work in and lead a group is critical at the child’s next step school and in later life.
This expertise is nurtured throughout the curriculum and manifests itself in the extensive range of activities our pupils take part in every week. Group and project work is the norm in our buzzing classrooms, as it is on the playing field, in our outdoor education programme and throughout our expeditions.
The children are encouraged to plan, choose ambitious but reasonable goals and stick to them. They learn to use their areas of strength to contribute to the group and leadership roles to harness them while committing to the venture even if they do not wholly agree with its direction. We ensure at every level of the school, such as in the school council, in positions of authority such as being a prefect or sports captain, we nurture these essential skills.
Independent and Reflective
Self-awareness, with the ability to assess oneself with a degree of impartially, is a great asset not only in education but also in adult life.
As we move towards the Prep School Baccalaureate (PSB) learning skills-based curriculum, we are making more time for this thoughtfulness and opportunities to self-reflect as it is a vital highly transferable skill. A child’s ability to appraise their own work effectively not only improves their ability to avoid repeating mistakes but increases their appreciation of the strength of others and what is worthy of imitation. We believe this independence of mind is an important foundation of original thinking and contributes to the other critical learning skills such as contributing individual insight productively to the many group and project sessions we build into their learning journey.
Where Next?

Head’s Welcome
West Hill Park is nestled in a unique rural setting on the doorstep of Titchfield and within easy reach of Portsmouth and Southampton.
Welcome to West Hill Park
West Hill Park is more than just a school, we are a vibrant community where every child has the chance to flourish. Our beautiful woodland, riding school, theatre, sports fields, and more create endless possibilities for exploration and growth.
Mr Chris Ward B.Ed. (Hons) Headmaster​
The world that awaits the children of today is changing. It is our role, in partnership with you as a parent, to prepare your child for the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.
West Hill Park provides a great diversity of opportunity for our pupils and a team of staff that deliver an outstanding level of pastoral care.
As we continue to develop the content and the application of the educational journey for your child, we focus on our key pillars of ambition, resilience and kindness, and the learning skills that harness these into developing a rounded, confident and happy student ready for adult life. In this way, we really feel we can provide your child with the very best start.
We offer both day and boarding options, and many of our pupils do both through our fun nights and flexi-boarding options. Boarders are a highly valued part of our school community.
In September 2025, we became part of Radley Schools Group, a ground-breaking group of eight charitable, independent schools. Radley Schools Group believes in the timeless and authentic values of high quality charitable independent education. Through the strength and stability of our group, we are committed to providing exceptional educational opportunities for all our pupils throughout their childhood. Blending the very best of tradition and innovation, we seek to develop young people of outstanding character and purpose for generations to come.
I warmly invite you to arrange a visit and experience our vibrant atmosphere in person. You’ll find a genuine welcome awaiting both you and your family.
Mr Chris Ward B.Ed. (Hons) Headmaster

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Prep School? - West Hill Park
pageCache.text:
Why Prep School?
Spanning the formative years
From ages 2 to 13, prep schools like West Hill Park offer a nurturing and secure environment where children can truly be themselves. We embrace the magic of childhood and actively protect it, allowing it to extend into the early teenage years.​
A Sense Of Belonging
At our school, it’s not uncommon to see Year 7 and 8 pupils playing alongside the younger children on the field. This cross-age interaction is part of what makes our community so special. It fosters empathy, responsibility, and a strong sense of belonging.
Meaningful Responsibilities
As pupils grow, we support them through the often-challenging early adolescent years by offering meaningful responsibilities such as mentoring younger pupils, leading school tours, and serving as role models for the wider school community. These opportunities help them step into their emerging identities with confidence, independence and kindness.
“I feel more mentally ready to transition to my new school – I have grown so much in confidence over the last two years. The leavers’ experience has helped me a lot in the transition from Prep to Senior school. Doing the PSB has really helped me as well – learning how to research and present.”
Where Next?

Music
Our Music Programme Includes
Specialist peripatetic teachers offer lessons in piano, voice, violin, cello, trumpet, trombone, guitar, ukulele, drum kit, flute, saxophone, recorder, and music theory. Approximately 160 individual lessons take place each week, with termly ABRSM examinations conducted on-site.
Opportunities for all students, including hymn practise on Mondays and during Wednesday assembly, singing during lessons, Junior Choir, Colla Voce Choir, Chamber Choir, School Orchestra, Rock Band (Years 6-8), Fiddlesticks (Years 3-4 String group), Woodwind, Brass, and Guitar Ensembles.
Termly instrumental concerts, informal concerts, jazz performances, Young Voices, Orchestral concerts, and Music tours including Disneyland Paris in 2025. Annual major productions for Years 5-8 (Spring term) and Years 3-4 (Summer term), alongside Pre-Prep and Prep Nativities (Autumn term). Additional performances include Harvest Festival, Remembrance Service, a traditional Carol service, and regular Open mic nights.
Developing musical literacy and creativity through traditional notation and digital composition tools.
Wealth of opportunity
From Orchestra to Open Mic Night, Colla Voce to Informal Concerts, Music Trips to Production. There are so many opportunities for pupils to flex their musical muscles and try new things!

pageCache.text:
Co-Curricular & Pastoral Care
Strong Pastoral Care
Each pupil has a form tutor who acts as the first point of contact for both academic and pastoral matters. Relationships are at the heart of life at West Hill Park, both between staff and pupils, and among peers. Through our PSHE programme, wellbeing initiatives, and clear values of kindness and respect, we create a community where every child can thrive.
An Unrivalled Co-Curricular Programme
Our Prep pupils are encouraged to find and follow their passions – both inside and outside the classroom. From music ensembles and drama productions to coding clubs, horse riding, debating, and outdoor pursuits, the breadth of opportunity is exceptional.
Our sports programme is equally inclusive and ambitious, with pupils representing the school in regular fixtures and developing skills in a wide range of disciplines including rugby, hockey, cricket, netball, swimming and athletics.
Outdoor Education
Outdoor learning remains a hallmark of a West Hill Park education. Building on the early years of Forest School, our Outdoor Education programme evolves through the Prep years, developing teamwork, leadership, and resilience.
As pupils move up the school, they take part in expeditions, adventure days, and survival skills training, culminating in our renowned Summer Expeditions. These challenges encourage independence and give our pupils a true sense of achievement and adventure.

Club WHP
A Diverse Range of Activities
Your children will be cared for by teachers and support staff from West Hill Park School. The programme is varied and we are lucky enough to have a very diverse range of activities delivered by teaching staff from across the school.
Welcome to Club WHP, West Hill Park School’s holiday camp for children aged 2.5–13 years. Set within the stunning grounds of West Hill Park School, Club WHP offers children the opportunity to enjoy exciting adventures, specialist activities and unforgettable experiences throughout the school holidays.
Children are cared for by West Hill Park’s teachers and support staff, with a programme designed and delivered by the school itself, powered operationally by Next Level Camps.
No two days are the same at Club WHP. Children can take part in a huge variety of activities including forest school, saddle club, performing arts, computing, sports, creative workshops and multi-activity days.
Throughout the year, specialist themed days and weeks provide unique opportunities such as paddleboarding, beach walks and outdoor adventures, making the most of the school’s exceptional facilities and location.
For those looking for even bigger adventures, selected holiday periods also feature exciting off-site trips to destinations such as Paultons Park, LEGOLAND and other local attractions.
Whether your child loves exploring the outdoors, getting creative, developing new skills or simply spending time with friends, Club WHP provides a safe, welcoming and engaging environment where every child can thrive.
Every day brings a new adventure at Club WHP.
Ages: 2.5–13 years
Time: 8:30am–5:00pm
Open to children from any school
Flexible booking options available
If you need any more information please email: clubwhp@westhillpark.org.uk

pageCache.text:
Scholarships & Bursaries
The tremendous diversity of opportunity we offer at West Hill Park allows all pupils the chance to find a space in which they can excel. To find out about Bursaries on offer, please visit the Radley Schools Group website here.
Pupils with a particular talent and potential in the arts, sport, sailing, riding or academically can apply for a Westhillian Scholarship to commence in the Autumn Term of Year 7 or Year 8. First and foremost, Scholarships are a recognition of a child’s talent and potential, with the aim of providing a springboard for scholarship attempts at chosen senior schools. A programme of support will be tailored specifically to help your child prepare for a scholarship at the senior school of your choice.
Types of Scholarship Available
All round Academic Scholarship
Sport Scholarship
Computing Scholarship
Ramsay Award for Sailing
Scholarship Award Conditions
Scholarships are attached to additional responsibilities for pupils. Westhillian Scholars are role models for their peers – sharing their knowledge, skills and passion with their fellow pupils.
Successful Scholars will be expected to fully engage in a programme to support their area of speciality to give them the very best chance of future scholarship success. Respective Heads of Departments will liaise with you and your child on activities and progress.
Application Process
If you wish to apply for a means-tested bursary, the application process will run alongside the scholarship assessments.
Scholarship Assessment
All candidates will also have a short interview with the relevant Head of Department, and an interview with the Senior Leadership Team.
In addition, it is expected that scholarship candidates have displayed consistently outstanding effort in their chosen curriculum area and have, prior to Year 7, demonstrated excellent commitment and potential for development.
All round Academic Scholarship
Maths and English paper under exam conditions
Arts Scholarships
Music
Drama
Sport Scholarship
Computing Scholarship
The Ramsay Award Scholarship for Sailing
Outcome
The highest band of achievers at the Scholarship Assessment stage will be awarded a scholarship to the school. A candidate who doesn’t quite reach scholarship standard may be awarded an Exhibition based on their performance. Full feedback will be provided by the Head of the relevant department.
Questions and Queries
Please direct any questions regarding the application process and means tested bursaries to Mr Ward.

Facilities Hire
Hire our facilities
West Hill Park offers a range of facilities for community hire, including a four-lane 25m pool, 2G astro pitch, theatre, sports hall, and more.
All hires are managed through a simple online system called School Hire.
On the system, you can view availability, ask us any questions and make your bookings.
Residential Hire
We also offer residential groups the opportunity to hire the full school site for certain periods in the Holidays – including our 70 bed boarding house, kitchens and access to our 28 acre site and woodlands. Just a 3 mile walk to the beach, and close to Southampton Airport – it’s an ideal location for many visiting groups. Please contact mbagnall@westhillpark.org.uk for residential booking enquiries.

Nursery
Our Nursery provision includes Little Griffins and Wild Griffins – giving you the flexibility to enjoy the wonder of Forest School alongside our inspiring nursery. Our children enjoy the benefits of being part of the wonderful West Hill Park School community, with access to over 25 acres of grounds and outstanding facilities.
Little Griffins is an all-year-round setting and welcomes children from 2. Families can split their child’s time between Little Griffins and Wild Griffins, our 100% outdoor forest school nursery. However, to give the forest time to recuperate, Wild Griffins will remain term-time only and will continue to be offered to children over 2.5. Pupils in Little Griffins enjoy specialist teaching including French, Swimming, Music, Art, Dance and Sport during our morning sessions, setting them up for a love of learning.
What age can children start at the Nursery?
Children can join Little Griffins from age 2, and Wild Griffins from 2.5.
What is the difference between Little Griffins and Wild Griffins?
Little Griffins offers a nurturing nursery environment within the school, while Wild Griffins provides outdoor Forest School nursery experiences. Children are encouraged to have days in both settings.
Is Little Griffins open all year?
Yes. Little Griffins offers all-year-round provision; Wild Griffins operates during term time.
What is Wild Griffins?
Wild Griffins is the outdoor Forest School nursery, where children learn through nature, exploration and play.
Can children attend both Little Griffins and Wild Griffins?
Yes. During term time, families can combine sessions across both settings, subject to availability.
Do Nursery children use the wider school facilities?
Nursery children benefit from being part of the wider school community and opportunities to use its facilities and benefit from specialist teaching.
Does West Hill Park accept Early Years funding?
West Hill Park participates in applicable government Early Years funding schemes up to 15 hours, we do not accept the 30 hours funding. Please contact our Head of Nursery for current eligibility and session arrangements.
